name: Malay Mishra

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Malay Mishra’s Odia poem ଭାବିନିଅ ଘୋର ବନସ୍ତରେ brings a tiger’s call into an argument about human pride and power. The speaker explicitly offers a human conjecture, asking whether the distant roar announces danger, desire or a claim to territory.

As the voice begins to inhabit the tiger’s authority, echoes become boundaries and the forest becomes a place of solitary possession. Questions give way to declarations, ending with an order for the jackals to leave. That changing voice, rather than a simple description of wildlife, gives the poem its force.
